Privacy policy

Last updated 24 October 2026.

Who is responsible

Harry James Coburn, contact details in the Impressum. Email: harry@harryjamescoburn.com.

No cookies, privacy-friendly statistics

This website sets no cookies and uses no advertising or cross-site tracking. Fonts are served from this website, not from a third party.

To see which pages are read and which links are clicked, I use Umami Cloud (Umami Software, Inc.), a cookieless analytics service. It records the page, the referring site, browser and device type, country and clicks on buttons such as "Book a call", without cookies and without storing your IP address or building a profile of you. The answers you give in the scorecard are not sent. The legal basis is my legitimate interest in understanding how the site is used (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). Umami's privacy policy applies.

Hosting and server logs

The site is hosted on GitHub Pages (GitHub, Inc., USA). When you visit, GitHub processes technical data such as your IP address, browser and the time of the request, to deliver the site and keep it secure. The legal basis is our legitimate interest in operating a secure website (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). See GitHub's privacy statement for details.

Booking a call

The “Book a call” buttons take you to my booking page on Cal.com (Cal.com, Inc.). If you book, Cal.com processes the name, email address and answers you enter, adds the meeting to my Google Calendar (Google Ireland Ltd) and creates a Google Meet link. I use them only to hold the call and follow up (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR). Cal.com's and Google's privacy policies apply to that processing.

The newsletter sign-up box is provided by Substack, Inc. It loads from Substack only on pages that show it. If you subscribe, Substack processes your email address to send you the newsletter, based on your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR). You can unsubscribe from any issue. Substack's privacy policy applies.

Scorecard report by email

If you ask for your scorecard report by email, the form sends your first name, email address, company and scorecard answers to a small script in my Google Workspace account (Google Ireland Ltd), which emails you the report from my own mailbox and records your details in my CRM, HubSpot (HubSpot, Inc., with data held in the EU). I use these details to send the report and an occasional follow-up, based on your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR), and to discuss working together if you want to. You can withdraw consent or ask me to delete your details at any time by emailing me. Google's and HubSpot's privacy policies apply.

If you arrived from a tracked link, the form also notes where you came from (for example LinkedIn), kept only for the length of your visit in your browser's session storage.

Talking to my AI assistant

The AI page has a voice and text assistant provided by ElevenLabs (Eleven Labs Inc.). It only loads when you click to start it. If you use it, ElevenLabs processes your voice or text and records the conversation so I can read it and reply. If you choose to give your name, email and company and agree that I may follow up, they are also saved in HubSpot. The legal basis is your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR). Please don't share sensitive information. ElevenLabs' privacy policy applies.

WhatsApp

The WhatsApp links only open a chat with my business number. Nothing is sent until you send a message yourself. If you do, WhatsApp (WhatsApp Ireland Ltd, part of Meta) processes it under its own privacy policy, and I use your number and message only to reply (Art. 6(1)(b) and (f) GDPR).

When you message or email me

If you use the message form, it sends your name, email, company and message to the same script in my Google Workspace account, which emails it to me and records it in HubSpot. If you contact me by message or email, I use your details only to reply and to discuss working together (Art. 6(1)(b) and (f) GDPR). I keep them only as long as needed for that, or as the law requires.

Your rights

You can ask for access to, correction or deletion of your data, restriction of or objection to its processing, and data portability (Art. 15 to 21 GDPR). You can also complain to a data protection authority, such as the Berlin Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information.
